newsitem.title: LITHUANIA: HERMIS BANK 1996 AUDITED PROFIT 27.4 MLN LITAS.
newsitem.headline: HERMIS BANK 1996 AUDITED PROFIT 27.4 MLN LITAS.

text.p: One of Lithuania's leading commercial banks Hermis Bank said on Thursday that its audited 1996 results showed a net profit of 27.4 million litas.
A bank spokesman said this compared with a profit in 1995 of five million litas.
The spokesman said net profit in 1995 was 3.6 million litas.
The share capital of Hermis increased three-fold in 1996 and is now 67 million litas.
The assets of the bank in 1996 rose by 68 percent to 534 milion litas at the end of the year, he added.
The bank said that it was the most profitable bank in Lithuania and that it would probably this year again pay dividends to shareholders.
The bank said in a short statement that net credits issued rose by 52 percent to 198 million litas from 130 million litas, which it said was due to a conservative credit policy.
It said that capital adequacy at the end of 1996 was 23.4 percent, nearly three times more than needed under central bank rules.
More than 75 percent of the share capital was owned by foreigners.
The number of clients and turnover rose, leading to a rise of clients funds held in bank accounts from 253 million litas to 395 million litas.
The bank said that it provided more sophisticated services, leading to a doubling of bank services revenue.
